content.text: In Nigeria, digital creators face a stark reality: Stripe, PayPal, and platforms like Teachable are unavailable. This isn't a temporary glitch—it's a structural exclusion. Your audience wants your courses, but conventional payment gateways block their purchases. Workarounds like VPN-based accounts or third-party processors fail under scrutiny. The real solution isn't another patch. It's sovereign commerce infrastructure—[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/real-architecture-behind-digital-product-payment-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/solutions-when-stripe-paypal-ban-account-which-architecture-7|Solutions When]]-west-2|architecture]] you own, control, and deploy without permission. This analysis compares your actual options for [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-courses-without-teachable-stripe-explained-digital-creators|COREMERCH guide to selling]] courses without depending on platforms that exclude you. We'll examine what each system delivers, how they handle restricted regions, their true costs, and who retains ownership. The goal is clear: identify the architecture that gives you permanent financial autonomy, not temporary access.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Courses teachable

Conventional platforms like Teachable bundle hosting, payment processing, and course delivery into a single interface. This works—until your country is blocked. Alternatives like Gumroad or Lemon Squeezy replicate this model but share the same dependency on Stripe or PayPal. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure decouples these layers. You host on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages (free), handle backend logic with Google Apps Script or Cloudflare Workers (free), store orders in Supabase or Google Sheets (free), and deliver files via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 (free). Payment processing uses NOWPayments, which accepts 300+ cryptocurrencies with a flat 0.5% fee and no KYC. The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) deploys this architecture in 48 hours, configured for five products, with SPF/DKIM/DMARC email security. The tradeoff is clear: convenience versus ownership. Platforms rent you access. Sovereign infrastructure gives you control.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Platforms like Teachable and Stripe exclude countries based on compliance, currency risk, or political sanctions. Their terms explicitly list restricted regions, and VPN-based workarounds violate their policies. Even if you bypass geolocation checks, payouts fail when your bank or identity verification flags your location. Sovereign commerce infrastructure avoids this by operating at the base layer. GitHub Pages, Cloudflare, and Supabase do not restrict access based on geography. NOWPayments processes crypto payments without requiring buyer accounts or KYC. The system is permissionless by design. For example, the Edge Commerce Stack deploys on globally accessible infrastructure, ensuring your store functions regardless of your location. The architecture is not a workaround—it's a structural alternative built for regions where conventional platforms refuse to operate.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Teachable charges 5% to 10% per transaction, plus Stripe's 2.9% + $0.30 fee. In restricted countries, these fees are irrelevant because you can't use them. Crypto payments via NOWPayments incur a flat 0.5% fee, with no monthly subscriptions or hidden costs. Transaction speeds depend on the blockchain network. BSC, Solana, and TRON confirm payments in seconds for under $0.10 per transaction. The Edge Commerce Stack integrates NOWPayments automatically, ensuring payments trigger file delivery instantly. The real cost comparison is stark: platforms charge recurring fees for rented access, while sovereign infrastructure requires a one-time investment. After deployment, your operational costs are near zero. The tradeoff is manual setup versus lifetime ownership.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure is permissionless by design—no platform can exclude you.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

With Teachable, your course data, customer list, and payment history belong to the platform. They can suspend your account or change their terms without notice. Sovereign infrastructure inverts this. You own the GitHub repository, Supabase database, and Cloudflare Workers code. Customer data is stored in systems you control. File delivery is automated via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, triggered by confirmed payments. The Edge Commerce Stack includes end-to-end testing to ensure this automation works flawlessly. After deployment, COREMERCH has no access to your system. You retain full ownership and control. The architecture is designed for creators who prioritize infrastructure sovereignty over platform convenience.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you operate in a restricted country and need permanent financial autonomy, sovereign commerce infrastructure is the only viable option. Platforms like Teachable and Stripe are not temporary inconveniences—they are structural exclusions. The Edge Commerce Stack provides a complete, deployed solution in 48 hours, configured for your specific needs. If you prefer renting access and can tolerate platform risks, conventional systems may suffice. But for creators in Nigeria, Ghana, Zimbabwe, and similar regions, this is not a choice. Sovereign infrastructure is not just an alternative—it's the base layer you build on. Choose architecture you own, not platforms that exclude you.

Integrate payment processing: NOWPayments (0.5% fee, no KYC). 6. Test end-to-end: Ensure payment confirmation triggers file delivery. 7. Deploy: Push your code to GitHub or Cloudflare. 8. Load products: Add your courses to the system. 9. Secure emails: Configure SPF/DKIM/DMARC if using email delivery. 10. Monitor: Track transactions and deliveries in your Supabase dashboard.
